chapter.title: Soap, organic surface-active agents, washing preparations, lubricating preparations, artificial waxes, prepared waxes, polishing or scouring preparations, candles and similar articles, modeling pastes, "dental waxes" and dental preparations with a basis of plaster

page.h1: HTS Chapter 34: Soap, organic surface-active agents, washing preparations, lubricating preparations, artificial waxes, prepared waxes, polishing or scouring preparations, candles and similar articles, modeling pastes, "dental waxes" and dental preparations with a basis of plaster — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Soap, Detergents & Lubricants by Country (HTS Ch. 34) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Canada, the EU, Mexico, China, Brazil, Japan, Singapore and Korea charge on U.S. soap, detergents, lubricants, waxes and candles, and the chemical registration each requires.
keywords: tariff on US soap by country

intro: Who buys U.S. soap, detergents, lubricants, waxes, polishes and candles, **what** they buy and **what they charge** on it. The matrix shows each market's tariff on U.S.-origin goods for the seven Chapter 34 product groups, next to the value the U.S. shipped there in 2025; the EU counts as one market because its members share one tariff. Canada, Mexico, Singapore, Korea and, since July 1, 2026, the EU charge nothing on qualifying U.S. goods, Japan charges only on lubricants, and Brazil charges the Mercosur tariff of up to 18%. China is the costly one, with its 10% extra tariff and 2018–2019 counter-tariffs. For detergents and lubricants the other gate is chemical and product registration in the buyer's market, named in each profile below.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

markets.name: Canada
markets.rule: CUSMA preferential tariff (United States Tariff, 0% on qualifying U.S. goods); Canada's 2025 surtax on U.S. soaps was repealed from September 1, 2025, and its 2026 surtax order lists no Chapter 34 goods

3401.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3401.11.90 and 3401.30.00: MFN 6.5%, United States Tariff Free. The 25% surtax of SOR/2025-66 applied from March 4 to August 31, 2025

3402.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3402.50.90, 3402.90.99 and 3402.42.90: MFN 6.5%, United States Tariff Free

3403.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3403.99.90 and 3403.19.99: MFN 6.5% (some items Free), United States Tariff Free

3404.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3404.90.90: MFN 6.5%, United States Tariff Free

3405.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3405.90.00: MFN 5.5%, United States Tariff Free

3406.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3406.00.90: MFN 5.5%, United States Tariff Free

3407.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026: 3407.00.10 and 3407.00.20 MFN 6.5%, 3407.00.90 Free; United States Tariff Free

profile.headline: Canada buys 37% of U.S. Chapter 34 exports and charges nothing on goods that qualify for CUSMA. U.S. soaps paid a 25% surtax from March 4 to August 31, 2025; nothing in the chapter is on Canada's September 2026 counter-tariff list.
profile.mainProducts: Surfactants, detergents & cleaners (3402) · Soap & skin-washing preparations (3401)

regulator.name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (New Substances, Phosphorus Concentration Regulations) and Health Canada
regulator.requirement: A chemical not on the Domestic Substances List must be notified under the New Substances Notification Regulations before import; household laundry detergents and dish-washing compounds may contain no more than 0.5% phosphorus by weight, and toilet soaps sold as cosmetics need a Health Canada Cosmetic Notification.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Canada import requirements

markets.name: European Union
markets.rule: EU–U.S. framework zero tariff (Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I lists all of Chapter 34) from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, replacing the EU common external tariff

3401.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I (Chapter 34), from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029; WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% for bar soap 3401.11 and 4% for liquid skin cleansers 3401.30 (2023) before that date

3402.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I (Chapter 34); WITS/TRAINS MFN 4% for 3402.50, 3402.90 and 3402.42 (2023) before July 1, 2026

3403.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I (Chapter 34); WITS/TRAINS MFN 4.6% for 3403.99 and 4.6–6.5% for 3403.19 (2023) before July 1, 2026

3404.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I (Chapter 34); WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% for 3404.90 (2023), so the rate did not change

3405.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I (Chapter 34); WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% for 3405.90 (2023)

3406.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I (Chapter 34); WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% for 3406.00 (2023)

3407.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I (Chapter 34); WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% for 3407.00 (2023)

profile.headline: The EU charges nothing on U.S. soap, detergents, lubricants, waxes and candles since July 1, 2026, down from 4% on detergents and 4.6–6.5% on lubricants. Its 2025 counter-tariff list named nearly the whole chapter but was never applied.

regulator.name: European Chemicals Agency (REACH, CLP) and the Detergents Regulation
regulator.requirement: Substances imported at 1 tonne a year or more must be registered under REACH by the EU importer or an Only Representative of the U.S. maker, mixtures must be classified and labelled under CLP, and surfactants in detergents must meet the biodegradability rules of Regulation (EC) No 648/2004.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: EU import requirements

markets.name: Mexico
markets.rule: USMCA preferential tariff (0% on qualifying U.S. goods); Mexico's general rates of 3–25% apply only to goods that do not qualify

3401.basis: LIGIE: 3401.11.01 15%; 3401.19.99, 3401.20.01 and 3401.30.01 raised to 25% by the December 29, 2025 decree; USMCA 0% for qualifying U.S. goods

3405.basis: LIGIE: 3405.90.99 15% (3405.40.01 raised to 25% from January 1, 2026); USMCA 0%

3407.basis: LIGIE: 3407.00.99 5%, dental waxes and plaster preparations Free; USMCA 0%

profile.headline: Mexico charges nothing on U.S. Chapter 34 goods that qualify for USMCA. Its general rate on soaps went up to 25% on January 1, 2026, which matters only for goods that do not meet the USMCA rules of origin.

regulator.name: COFEPRIS and the Ministry of Economy (NOM-189-SSA1/SCFI-2018)
regulator.requirement: Household cleaning products such as detergents and dish soaps must be labelled and packaged under NOM-189-SSA1/SCFI-2018, in force since December 13, 2019; confirm any further permit with the importer of record.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Mexico import requirements

markets.name: China
markets.rule: China's MFN tariff schedule (2026), plus the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods (since May 2025) and its 2018–2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (answering U.S. Section 301), which apply unless the importer holds an exclusion

3401.basis: China 2026 tariff: MFN 6.5% on 3401; + 10% on all U.S. goods; + 2019 counter-tariff of 25% on bar soap 3401.11 and 3401.20, 10% on liquid skin cleansers 3401.30 (Announcement No. 3 of 2019) unless excluded

3402.basis: MFN 6.5% on 3402; + 10%; + counter-tariff of 25% on non-ionic 3402.42 (List 2, 2018), 20% on washing powder 3402.50.10, 10% on 3402.50.90 and 3402.90, 5% on anionic and cationic surfactants, unless excluded

3403.basis: MFN 10% on 3403; + 10%; + 25% counter-tariff on 3403.19 and 3403.99 (List 2, from August 23, 2018) and on 3403.91 (20% on 3403.11); their product exclusion ended February 28, 2025

3404.basis: MFN 10% on 3404; + 10%; + counter-tariff of 10% on 3404.90 and 5% on polyethylene glycol waxes 3404.20 (Announcement No. 3 of 2019) unless excluded

3405.basis: MFN 6.5% on 3405; + 10%; + counter-tariff of 10% on 3405.20–3405.90 and 20% on shoe polish 3405.10 unless excluded

3406.basis: MFN 6.5% on 3406.00; + 10%; + counter-tariffs of 5% (2019 Annex 4) and 2.5% (September 2019 list, halved in February 2020) unless excluded

3407.basis: MFN 6.5% on dental waxes and plaster preparations, 10% on other modelling pastes (3407.0090); + 10%; + counter-tariff of 10% on 3407.0010, 25% on 3407.0020 and 20% on 3407.0090 unless excluded

profile.headline: China is the most expensive large market: U.S. lubricating preparations pay about 45% and non-ionic surfactants and bar soap 41.5%, after their product exclusion lapsed in February 2025. U.S. sales there fell 9% in 2025 and another 20% in January–August 2026.

regulator.name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (new chemical substance registration, Order No. 12)
regulator.requirement: A chemical substance not on China's inventory, such as a new surfactant or lubricant base stock, needs environmental-management registration before import; from August 15, 2026 MEE no longer accepts record-filing for new substances and uses a simplified registration instead.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: China import requirements

markets.name: Brazil
markets.rule: Mercosur common external tariff (MFN); no trade agreement with the U.S. and no counter-tariff on U.S. goods

3401.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN (Mercosur common external tariff) 18% on 3401.11, 3401.19, 3401.20 and 3401.30 (2023)

3402.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 18% on retail washing preparations (HS 2017 3402.20), 14% on non-ionic surfactants (3402.13), 2–18% on 3402.90 (2023)

profile.headline: Brazil has no trade agreement with the U.S., so U.S. goods pay the Mercosur tariff: 14% on lubricants, 18% on soaps and retail detergents. It has imposed no counter-tariff on U.S. goods.

regulator.name: ANVISA (household cleaning products) and ANP (lubricants)
regulator.requirement: Household cleaning products (saneantes) such as detergents must be notified to or registered with ANVISA before sale, and lubricating oils and greases must be registered with the ANP by the producer or importer under Resolution ANP 804/2019.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Brazil import requirements

markets.name: Japan
markets.rule: Japan's MFN tariff; the U.S.–Japan agreement did not change Japan's tariffs on these goods

3403.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 3.1% on 3403.99, 3.2% on 3403.19 and 4.4% on textile-treatment preparations 3403.11 and 3403.91 (2023)

profile.headline: Japan charges nothing on U.S. soap, detergents, waxes, polishes and candles and 3.1–4.4% on lubricating preparations. Exports there rose 12% in 2025.

regulator.name: METI, MHLW and MOE (Chemical Substances Control Law)
regulator.requirement: A new chemical substance must be notified and evaluated before manufacture or import under the Chemical Substances Control Law, and imported existing substances are reported by volume.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Japan import requirements

markets.name: Singapore
markets.rule: Singapore charges no import duty on these goods (MFN 0%); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

3401.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% on every 3401 line (2023); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

3402.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% on every 3402 line (2023); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

3403.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% on every 3403 line (2023); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

3404.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% on every 3404 line (2023); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

3405.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% on every 3405 line (2023); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

3406.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% on every 3406 line (2023); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

3407.basis: WITS/TRAINS MFN 0% on every 3407 line (2023); the U.S.–Singapore FTA also gives 0%

profile.headline: Singapore charges nothing on any Chapter 34 good, and much of what it buys, especially lubricants, is re-exported across Southeast Asia.

regulator.name: National Environment Agency (hazardous substances)
regulator.requirement: Hazardous substances listed under the Environmental Protection and Management Act need an NEA licence and import permit; most finished soaps, detergents and lubricants are not on the list.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Singapore import requirements

markets.name: South Korea
markets.rule: KORUS FTA preferential tariff (0% on qualifying U.S. goods); MFN of 2–8% for goods that do not qualify

3401.basis: KORUS 0% for qualifying U.S. goods; WITS/TRAINS MFN 6.5% on 3401.11–3401.30 (2023)

3402.basis: KORUS 0%; WITS/TRAINS MFN 5–6.5% on 3402.50 and 3402.90, 2–8% on 3402.42, 8% on anionic and cationic surfactants (2023)

profile.headline: Korea charges nothing on U.S. Chapter 34 goods that qualify for KORUS, against an MFN rate of 6.5–8%. Exports there fell 15% in 2025.

regulator.name: Ministry of Environment (K-REACH and household chemical products)
regulator.requirement: New chemical substances, and existing substances imported at 1 tonne a year or more, must be registered under K-REACH, usually through a Korean importer or only representative; household detergents and cleaners also need a safety check under Korea's household chemical products law.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: South Korea import requirements

assumptions: Rates are for 2026, one representative six-digit subheading per product group, usually the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports (shown under each cell): Canada from the CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, the EU from Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Mexico from its LIGIE schedule as amended by the December 29, 2025 decree, and China from its 2026 Customs Tariff. Brazil, Japan, Korea and Singapore, and the EU's pre-July 2026 rates, are WITS/TRAINS MFN applied rates for 2023, the latest year available. National 8–10-digit lines can differ.

The EU is one market: its 27 members share one tariff, and its export figures include every member. Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes out all of Chapter 34 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, on proof of U.S. origin; the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before then. The Commission can suspend the cut.
Canada, Mexico (USMCA) and Korea (KORUS) apply 0% to U.S.-origin goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; the normal-rate column shows the MFN rate for goods that do not qualify.

China's cells add three layers: its MFN rate, its 2018–2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (the List 2 rate of 2018 or the June 2019 rate, plus any September 2019 rate, halved in February 2020) and the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods. An importer holding a market-based exclusion (valid until December 31, 2026) pays only the MFN rate plus 10%. A further 24 points of the extra duty are suspended until January 10, 2027.

Pure lubricating oils with 70% or more petroleum oil are classified in heading 2710 (Chapter 27), not here; Chapter 34 lubricants are greases, synthetic and silicone lubricants and preparations with less than 70% petroleum oil.
Rates are import duties only; VAT, GST and excise are left out. Regulatory requirements are summarised for orientation; check the regulator's current rules for the specific product.
